terra.problem: Calling the daughter an only child adds that Jairus had no other children. The text says only that she was his only daughter.
Matthew 8:5-6 describes the centurion's request, but does not establish that Jesus helped his servant. The healing is in Matthew 8:13.
Saying the girl was just about to be grown adds a detail the text does not give.
“Four years off is a big gap” draws negative attention to the baker's missed answer.
The statement that sacrifices were part of life at the time brings in a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The text says she touched the fringe. It does not say whether she grabbed or tugged it.
The text does not say that the woman never went near Jesus' sandals.
The text does not say the woman was hiding in the crowd.
The explanation is flat and generic. Peter's observation about the pressing crowd offers a clear opening for Papa Dorin's warmth and humor.
The text says Jesus knew power had gone out from Him, not what He felt. It also does not say that only one touch carried power.
The text does not say the woman had been hiding.
Calling this the hardest news Jairus could hear states an assessment of his experience as fact.
The text says only those named were allowed to go in with Jesus. It does not say the rest stayed outside the house.
Five people were allowed to go in with Jesus, but saying there were five people with Him in the room leaves out the girl.
The passage does not say how soon after these words the girl gets up. It says she gets up at once after Jesus calls to her.
Saying Jesus' words made no sense to the mourners adds their unreported thoughts as fact.
The text does not say what the mourners had seen or that Jesus' words sounded laughable to them.
The text does not say everyone in the room could not believe what happened.
Luke records Jesus' command, but the text does not say He spoke no other words around it.
Saying Jesus thought of the girl's next need assigns Him an unreported thought and reason.
The text does not say that something to eat was close at hand.
